item.title: The Shape You Can Grade: Hexagonal Architecture for AI-Written Code
item.description:
Generating code stopped being the bottleneck. Checking it didn’t.

An AI agent produces a working feature in minutes. It also produces features whose tests pass and whose shape is wrong. A use case imports a database driver. A domain type depends on an HTTP client. Nothing fails. The suite is green. The next change is a little harder, and the one after that is harder still.

A test suite answers one question: does it run? Nothing in the usual loop answers the second one: is it still the system I designed? In Inside the AI Harness I argued that the checks, not the prompts, are what let you trust an agent’s work. This post is about a check for design itself, and the tool I built to run it.
